steps.text: Identifies the indication for administering oxygen therapy via a Hudson mask.
Performs hand hygiene.
Introduces self and establishes rapport.
Performs a respiratory assessment if baseline data is not available.
Checks that oxygen has been prescribed by a doctor. If there is no order, uses clinical judgement to decide if oxygen is required.

steps.text: Prepares the equipment: oxygen supply, Hudson mask, tubing.
Provides safety education about oxygen therapy to the person and family.
Performs hand hygiene.
Explains why oxygen therapy is required and gains consent.
Assists the person into a semi-Fowler's position if possible.
Connects the oxygen tubing to the flow meter outlet and to the mask.
Connects and sets up a humidifier if required.
Turns the oxygen on and checks it is functioning properly.
Guides the mask to the person's face and applies it from the nose downwards.
Fixes the mask to the contours of the person's face.
Secures the elastic around the person's head so the mask stays in place.
Applies padding if required to protect ears and bony prominences.
Attaches a pulse oximetry probe and sets both low and high alarms.
Performs hand hygiene.
Assesses the person's facial skin for dampness or chafing.
Checks the delivery device regularly and troubleshoots any problems.
Monitors oxygen saturation regularly or as ordered by the doctor.
Checks and ensures all documentation is completed.
Communicates any changes in the findings to the treating doctor.

Perform or review a respiratory assessment and baseline observations.

notes.text: Lab 2 is assessed with the Section 12.5 clinical skills appraisal forms for the Hudson, non-rebreather and Venturi masks. Each is marked U (unsatisfactory), D (developing), S (satisfactory) or NA.

Flow ranges on the 93225 Canvas page: nasal prongs 1-4 L of O2, and anything above 4 L needs humidification, which standard prongs can't provide. Hudson mask 5-10 L. Section 12.5 gives different ranges (see the next note and CONFLICTS).

Section 12.5 device ranges: nasal cannula 24-44% at 1-6 L/min (about 4% more per L/min; humidification may be recommended above 4 L/min; above 6 L/min FiO2 does not increase). Simple face mask 40-60% at 5-8 L/min, with a minimum of 5 L/min to prevent rebreathing CO2. Non-rebreather 95-100% at 10-15 L/min; the bag must not totally deflate. Venturi 24-50% at 4-10 L/min (e.g. blue adaptor 24% at 4 L/min; green 35% at 8 L/min).

TSANZ SpO2 targets: 88-92% in chronic respiratory disease with potential for hypercapnia (give O2 when SpO2 < 88%); otherwise 92-96% (give O2 when SpO2 < 92%). Senior clinician review if FiO2 ≥ 0.40 or ≥ 6 L/min via simple face mask is needed to keep the target; ICU review if FiO2 ≥ 0.50 or ≥ 8 L/min via simple face mask.

Device safety points from the Lab 2 workbook: nasal prongs, check nares/ears; Hudson, ensure appropriate flow and fit; Venturi, use the prescribed adaptor/setting and maintain target saturation; non-rebreather, the reservoir must be inflated before applying to the face.
